newsitem.title: USA: Input/Output bounces back from tumble.
newsitem.headline: Input/Output bounces back from tumble.

text.p: Shares in seismic survey company Input/Output Inc bounced back on Thursday from a sharp drop caused by a worse-than-expected earnings forecast.

The Stafford, Texas, company's shares rose three points, or 18.6 percent, to 19-1/8 in early afternoon. Input/Output had the sharpest percentage rise on the New York Stock Exchange and volume also led the market at 6.7 million shares.

Analysts said the market had overreacted on Wednesday when Input/Output's shares fell 7-1/2 to 16-3/8. The drop came after the company said its second-quarter earnings and revenues would be below expectations because of delays in equipment sales talks.
"It got bombed yesterday," said George Gaspar, an analyst with Robert W. Baird in Milwaukee.
"I think yesterday was an overreaction. There are a lot of people who are interested in the company."

Gaspar said his firm had cut its earnings forecast for Input/Output. Its earnings per share (EPS) estimate for fiscal 1997 was cut to $0.87 from $1.20, and the EPS estimate for fiscal 1998 was trimmed to $1.30 from $1.60.
The fiscal years end in May.
